name: Files
about: A tree of the project down the side, which you can browse and rearrange
_about: The worked example of a plugin that changes the editor's shape rather
than only its contents. A column pinned down the left, at a width of
its own, collapsed with the same key that opened it — all of it from a
plugin, with no change to textfold.
Then `files` in the palette, or bind the key it suggests (Alt-1).
Running it again puts it away, which is what collapsible means from a
`dock` is the whole of the difference between this and cargo's report
panel. Declared here rather than announced by the program, so the
editor can lay it out before this has ever been started; a plugin that
wants to move or resize it while running can say so with `panel/dock`.
It renames and deletes through the editor — `file/rename`, not `mv` —
because a buffer open on a file that was renamed underneath it is a
buffer that will save to the old name, and a language server still
being told about a path that no longer exists. Only the editor can fix
that, so only the editor should be doing it.
